input: nums is a Array of n nonnegative integers in [0, 9007199254740990], with 0 <= n <= 4294967295. The sum of all entries must be <= 9007199254740991. Duplicates and arbitrary order are accepted. Integers are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessor-backed elements; strings are primitive, not boxed. No concurrent mutation, getters or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds are not a guarantee of available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The maximum integer points obtainable by repeatedly choosing a present value v, earning v and removing that occurrence plus every occurrence of v-1 and v+1. Equal remaining v occurrences may all be chosen. Empty/all-zero input returns 0. The method returns optimal points, not a deletion schedule.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs, ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state. The deletion game is modeled, not performed on nums. A private map aggregates gains for each value, and a new sorted key sequence drives two rolling DP states. No mutable result container is returned.
numeric: The one-unit upper margin makes previous+1 safe. Every grouped gain and DP sum combines disjoint nonnegative contributions and is bounded by the declared total input sum; bounding only the final answer would not suffice for arbitrary values. JavaScript key sorting uses relational comparison, not subtraction. Zero gains remain valid map entries.
complexity: O(n + u + 1) map/DP operations for u distinct values, plus sorting. JavaScript key sorting adds T_sort(u) time and O(u+S_sort(u)) auxiliary map/key storage; ECMAScript does not impose universal sort complexity. Expected map-operation costs remain runtime assumptions: no universal ECMAScript constant-time Map guarantee is claimed. The recurrence combines only the old skip state when consecutive values conflict, otherwise the old best; no dense array up to the maximum value is allocated.
